title: Concerning the Four great Things
text:
⟨p.118⟩
46
— Concerning the Four —
46 Great Works 46
Once again the Illuminator said: The wheel of the stars which
is manifest unto you — it is a great mighty work; it itself is
one of the Four Great Works, since the archonic
host in its entirety has been distributed into four kinds.
The first kind is the powers that exist in the ten firma-
ments that exist on the upper side of the wheel, with the archon-
ic host that is bound within them, chosen into them, in the heav-
ens that are on the upper side.
The second kind is
the eight earths on the lower side, the four that are joined
with the four places of the Darkness; the second kind
is from this earth on which men walk down unto
the lower side.
The third kind is the {9}-
ations and the strongholds that surround the worlds, which
are the four of them with the three strongholds
and that which is within them, with the archonic host that is gathered into them,
with the powers that are lord over them.
The fourth{10}
kind is the sphere of stars that {11} in a {12}
shame, being heavy in a {13}
great-she-is; the Father of {14}Life {15}
⟨p.119⟩
the Living Ones. Her lash {0} ...-ed, raised up in shame,
because of the great powers of concupiscence and the shamelessnesses {1}
in her, being many upon her, so that all the firstborn and the
principalities of all the archons, those who were existing in the third
kind: those whom they bound, they gathered them in, they reckoned them,
they bound them, they fixed them in this Wheel, they appointed each one
each one in the third kind: they spread them forth, they {2} them,
they hung them facing one another in single accord — the {3}
likewise is equal with them in his might, in the {4} of
Enmity that is bound in him — those whom they hung {5} in {6}
Wheel that turns, because of their concupiscence, so that {7}
the Spirit and the fire that turn there in him, they were
abiding at the place where they stand fast in him. For thus, again, if
they had been bound in the heavens, the heavens would (not) have power
to bear them, no. Were they fixed again in the lands, in the
mountains which are below, neither would they be able to bear them;
but they hung them upon the Wheel of stars that turns, so that
the power and the light that ascends forth from the lower
side — they receive it with them and give it to those above, {8}
there. And that which falls also from the upper side,
whether it be in the cold or rather in the heat — the Wheel
of the sphere too shall lift it up to him and shall cast it forth
upon the whole earth, upon the whole tree. Behold, this is the appointment
in this manner of the Wheel; for the powers that are bound in the
Wheel are likened in this manner: they reigned to seize his
kingship in the multitude of mighty Aeons, of all the
principalities of the kingship, and with the whole garment
{9} the love-of-strife that is gathered into him, and also with
{10} multitude of {11}, and the kingship, and the beautiful likeness
{12} desire of {13}, that is gathered into him together with
{14} property {15} and those animals there, being
{16} {17} which were spread forth from his hunger
⟨p.120⟩
comitatus. Yet if you inquire after this king, he is equal
with his whole comitatus. The comitatus itself
is equal against his whole kingship. A matter habitually comes forth before
his face — a victory and an appointment — unto his whole kingship,
in his wisdom, in his skill, in his judiciousness.
According therefore to the manner of this king who is equal against the measure of his entire
kingship — in his wisdom, in his skill, and his
judiciousness.
In this same manner, according to this likening of the
realms which are bound in the sphere before the archonic host, and the
realms which exist in the entire Zone — thus is the king to his entire
comitatus. In this same manner indeed the whole work is gathered
to the sphere, to the seven guides, to the twelve zo-
diac signs — thus all the cities are gathered to the king, being also gathered
to the way-leaders of the world — that which they reckon entirely, all of it,
in the world of the upper region and of the lower region — the strifes
and the disturbances and the captivity and the hunger and the de-
sire and the property which they multiply and they diminish through
the way-leaders. They are the movers of the entire creation,
the whole work being gathered into them, according to the manner I have spoken
to you — I have made (it) known forth to you. —
